item.title: Mitchell, Tractable Plan Automated Collision Intake Integration
item.description: The planned integration is intended to give North American multi-site operators (MSOs) and independent collision repair centers an automated path from vehicle intake and damage documentation to creation of a preliminary repair estimate. (Image source: Tractable LumaScanner page.) Mitchell (San Diego) plans to expand its collaboration with Tractable (London) through a proposed exclusive agreement connecting Tractable’s LumaScanner automated vehicle inspection system with Mitchell Intelligent Estimating. “Our goal is to help collision repairers simplify the vehicle intake process by connecting innovative technologies that are designed to optimize key steps in the workflow,” comments Olivier Baudoux, SVP, Global Product Strategy and Artificial Intelligence, Mitchell.

item.title: Amdocs Enters Insurance With $340 Million EIS Acquisition
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Amdocs (Jersey City, N.J.) has acquired EIS (San Francisco) for approximately $340 million in cash, making its first entry into the insurance industry and establishing the sector as a strategic growth and diversification market. “The EIS acquisition gives Amdocs a credible entry into insurance, where carriers face the same legacy billing and policy challenges that Amdocs has tackled for telecom operators for decades,” comments Karlyn Carnahan, Executive Partner, Celent. “The move also reflects a clear push to diversify beyond a telecom market where growth is increasingly hard to find.” Carnahan characterizes the $340 million acquisition as “a modest, long-term bet,” adding that its success will depend on whether Amdocs can demonstrate that its telecom-developed aOS platform resonates with insurers in a crowded core-systems market.

item.title: Flarre.AI Names Sokal VP of AI and Products
item.description: (Aasim Kumar Sokal, VP, AI and Products, Flarre.AI. Source: Flarre.AI.) Flarre.AI (Tampa, Fla.) has appointed Aasim Kumar Sokal VP of AI and Products, giving him responsibility for the company’s AI, product and platform strategy. In his new role, Sokal will help translate carrier requirements and market needs into platform capabilities and identify new areas for product development as Flarre.AI expands its insurance-native agentic AI platform.

item.title: New APCIA Initiative Looks to Help ‘Backbone’ of Industry With Regulatory Costs
item.description: “Collectively they give our private competitive marketplace much of the depth, specialization and resilience that it enjoys.” However, discussions with 20 small and medium carriers on APCIA’s board confirmed there is a need to reduce regulatory costs that are amounting to what Bell described as a “scale tax” that is paid “not because the company presents more risk, but because it has fewer premium dollars across which to spread a largely fixed cost.” “Delays in approvals, filings or licensing, costly and inconsistently applied state exam formats – they don’t just cost money, they cost opportunity,” Bell said, adding that when the admitted market becomes slower, capital and product innovation migrate to the excess and surplus lines market – a “structural rather than situation” migration. APCIA’s proposed Small and Medium Sized Insurer Regulatory Cost Initiative (SMSIRCI) will work to pursue regulatory improvements and benefits for carriers that will hopefully trickle to consumers once changes positively affect the expense ratios of small and medium-sized carriers. Small and midsize carriers “form the backbone” of the private insurance market, and they are being bogged down by the cost of regulatory and corporate compliance.

item.title: The Latest Launches from Insurify, Insurity
item.description: Insurify, an online insurance marketplace, announced the launch of its AI Agent Gateway with the aim of giving consumers a faster, more efficient way to shop for insurance using their personal AI agents. The gateway connects AI agents directly to Insurify’s marketplace so a shopper’s agent can gather and compare real-time quotes while preserving information and safeguards essential to choosing coverage. The launch builds on Insurify’s introduction of a ChatGPT plugin for insurance shopping.

item.title: Crunchbase Data: Less Than 2% Of 2026 Venture Funding Went To Post-Election Red States
item.description: So far this year, less than 2% of all startup investment has gone to companies in post-election red states, defined as those that will have both a Republican governor and two Republican U.S. This year, as of Election Day, startups in the remaining 17 red states 1 , which are home to nearly a quarter of Americans, had collectively pulled in just $8.6 billion in venture funding, with Florida, Tennessee and Utah among the largest contributors. Beyond the aforementioned newcomers Texas and Ohio, several other purple states regularly pull in sizable venture funding, including Pennsylvania, North Carolina and to some extent Wisconsin.

item.title: AIG expects a ‘good balance’ between front-end pressures and reinsurance savings at 1.1, says CEO
item.description: Eric Andersen, President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of global insurer AIG, expects the carrier to find a good balance between some of the front-end pressures in the property insurance space and the ability to save money on its reinsurance buying at the January 1 renewals. “So, I think we’re going to get a good balance between some of the front-end pressure and some of the ability to save money on some of the reinsurance support,” added Andersen. Clearly, AIG’s reinsurance strategy has played a pivotal role in its journey to become a leading global P&C underwriter, and with conditions expected to remain favourable for buyers at the upcoming 1.1 renewals, Andersen expects the company to benefit from further cost savings.

item.title: Data centres won’t move the needle on insurance sector top line: Autonomous
item.description: Analysts at Autonomous said they do not expect the data centre trade to move the needle for the insurance sector, suggesting the opportunity set will add just ~1% to the overall commercial P&C market through 2030, despite the hype. In a recent report, analysts at Autonomous estimate that new premiums across lines related to data centres will be worth $9 billion to $12 billion by 2030, which is significantly below other estimates. However, Autonomous said it has started to see cracks in this notion, partly because of concerns over insurance coverage.

item.title: Aon reports wider insurance buyer options as capacity grows and pricing eases
item.description: Aon suggested that this wider distribution of capital could make the market less dependent on individual sources of capacity and provide additional options for businesses seeking insurance protection. Increased underwriting capacity and competition between insurers helped maintain favourable trading conditions across much of the global commercial insurance market in the third quarter of 2026, according to Aon, a global professional services firm providing risk management, insurance broking and advisory services. Pricing in casualty insurance also moved downwards across markets outside the US.

item.title: Oklahoma Approves 4.8% Decrease in Workers’ Comp Loss Costs
item.description: Oklahoma Insurance Commissioner Glen Mulready announced that the Oklahoma Insurance Department (OID) has approved a 4.8% decrease in workers’ compensation insurance loss costs for 2027. Insurers use these costs as a key factor when calculating workers’ compensation premiums, so lower loss costs can help reduce insurance expenses for Oklahoma employers. NCCI is authorized to make recommended loss-cost filings on behalf of workers’ compensation insurance companies in Oklahoma and 37 other states.

item.title: State of Emergency Declared After Flooding, Two Deaths on Florida’s East Coast
item.description: Florida’s governor declared a state of emergency for seven counties after three days of extreme rainfall caused flooding in Brevard, DeSoto, Hardee, Highlands, Indian River, Martin and St. The “1-in-1,000-year” event, as it was described by the National Weather Service, produced almost 24 inches of rain at Malabar in a 24-hour period; almost 20 inches at Palm Bay; and 13 inches in and around Melbourne, on Florida’s east coast, the Florida Today news site reported . Ron DeSantis’ emergency declaration helps pave the way for state and federal assistance for municipalities and residents affected by the floods.

item.title: South Dakota Aquifers in Decline, Threatening Fresh Water Supplies
item.description: Geologists and hydrologists can use scientific charts and graphs to understand the increasing water challenges facing South Dakota, but it only takes a brief visit to Bear Butte State Park near Sturgis for a non-scientist to see the outcome of decreasing water levels. For the past several years in South Dakota, the combined effects of rising population, long-range drought and increased residential, commercial and agricultural water use are causing water shortages across the state. The lake that forms the centerpiece of the state park is usually a 215-acre expanse of fresh water that extends 15 feet deep and is home to walleye, crappie and catfish as well as an array of waterfowl and wildlife.

item.title: Approximately $340m deal sees Amdocs acquire insurance core platform provider EIS
item.description: The post Approximately $340m deal sees Amdocs acquire insurance core platform provider EIS appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Amdocs has acquired EIS, the San Francisco-based insurance core platform provider, for approximately $340m in cash, according to the release. The deal marks the first step into the insurance industry for Amdocs, the telecoms software and services provider listed on NASDAQ under the ticker DOX.

item.title: BPCE Assurances agrees to acquire GamaLife from Apax Funds
item.description: BPCE Assurances has agreed to acquire GamaLife, a life insurer operating in Portugal and Italy, from Apax Funds. In BPCE Assurances we have a partner with the scale and long-term commitment to support the next stage of the business, and our focus on serving our clients and distribution partners to the highest standard as we move forward.” GamaLife was carved out of novobanco, where it operated as GNB Vida, by Apax Funds in 2019, and in 2022 it acquired Zurich's Italian life and pensions business. Groupe BPCE announced on 3 November that it has signed a memorandum of understanding with Apax Funds and entered exclusive negotiations for 100% of GamaLife's share capital.

item.title: Demo: ScienceSoft
item.description: ScienceSoft's agentic solution matches P&C claim details against policy documents and delivers evidence-backed coverage conclusions in minutes while keeping adjusters in control of final decisions ScienceSoft's AI Agent for P&C Claims Coverage Verification adapts to your existing operations and technology landscape rather than forcing you to work around the software. ScienceSoft can customize the agent's verification logic, workflows, and outputs to reflect your coverage policies, authority levels, and claims handling practices. Watch the demo to see the agent verify coverage for a homeowners hail damage claim.

item.title: Marsh plans captive insurance services in Bahrain
item.description: Marsh plans to expand its Bahrain business to include captive insurance management services, which it says would make it the first international broker to offer those services in the country. Marcin Antosik, Captive Regional Leader for the Middle East, will lead the Bahrain offering alongside Marsh’s other captive operations in the region. The expansion follows Marsh’s receipt of captive insurance licenses in Dubai in 2008 and Abu Dhabi in 2018.

item.title: Mitchell plans Tractable vehicle inspection integration
item.description: Mitchell announced plans to expand its collaboration with Tractable through a proposed exclusive agreement to integrate Tractable’s LumaScanner vehicle inspection system with Mitchell Intelligent Estimating. The offering would complement Mitchell’s existing mobile photo-capture tools, giving repairers another way to document vehicle damage at intake. The integration would serve collision repair chains and independent repair centers in North America, generating preliminary repair estimates for appraisers to review and edit.

item.title: Aon launches healthcare Risk Capital vertical
item.description: Aon has launched a North America Healthcare vertical within its Risk Capital business, bringing together its healthcare liability reinsurance and commercial risk practices to serve U.S. Nick Gaudiosi has been appointed to lead the vertical as North America Healthcare Industry Leader, Risk Capital. The team will help clients assess risk and determine how to finance it through insurance, reinsurance, captives and alternative capital.

item.title: Act now to be resilient in the quantum future
item.description: Quantum computing will bring significant opportunities to the UK financial sector, but firms need to act now to prepare for a world where a viable hostile quantum computer could break today’s widely used cryptography standards. Sufficiently powerful quantum computers pose a real threat to that security. That’s why we are talking to firms about preparing for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) now.

item.title: Most Venture Capital Is Going To Companies That Are Founded Or Led By Billionaires
item.description: venture capital nowadays goes to companies founded or led by men who are already billionaires. So far this year, just seven companies raised more than half of all seed- through growth-stage investment. These companies raised more than $260 billion in equity funding in the first 10 months of the year.

item.title: Alternative capital driving greater options for insurance buyers: Aon
item.description: The expansion of alternative and institutional capital alongside traditional reinsurance is helping expand program choice for insurance buyers, according to broker Aon’s Q3 2026 Global Insurance Market Insights report. According to Aon, strong reinsurer balance sheets and favourable treaty renewals are being supplemented by committed, multi-year institutional and alternative capital, giving clients more options to structure their insurance programs and access capacity. As more capital competes for well-managed risks, clients with strong data and a clear narrative can be more deliberate about who they partner with, and on what terms.” The broker emphasises that the choice extends heavily beyond traditional insurance, with clients increasingly turning toward captives, structured solutions, parametric products and other alternative risk transfer options for extra flexibility.

item.title: SafePoint secures its largest catastrophe bond ever, $650m Nature Coast Re 2026-2
item.description: SafePoint Insurance Company has successfully secured its largest catastrophe bond yet, as the Nature Coast Re Ltd. (Series 2026-2) issuance marks the largest catastrophe bond that SafePoint Insurance Company has ever sponsored. Special purpose insurer (SPI) Nature Coast Re will now issue two tranches of Series 2026-2 catastrophe bond notes to source reinsurance for SafePoint Insurance Company itself and the two reciprocal exchanges it operates.

item.title: Axor Financial launched as $1bn insurance capital platform by Cohen. Hires Fox from HCMA
item.description: Axor Financial has been launched with a vision to provide the right capital into the insurance and reinsurance industry, with the new business that has been founded by former Gallatin Point exec Zhak Cohen recognising the need for alignment between capital providers and the industry participants they are funding. Axor Financial explains itself as, “A $1 billion principal capital platform dedicated to insurance — marrying flexible, long-term capital with insurance focus and expertise.” Founder Zhak Cohen has a wealth of experience investing in and deploying a wide-range of capital solutions to the insurance and reinsurance markets. When he launched Axor Financial Cohen explained, “The premise is simple: insurance does not lack capital; it lacks the right capital—capital of the appropriate form and quality, committed for the right duration, available at meaningful scale, and backed by a deep understanding of the businesses and risks it supports.

item.title: Trackers are not for us. When the market softens you’ve got to underwrite: Lancashire CEO
item.description: Lancashire Holdings’ CEO Alex Maloney explained this morning that when the market is softening actively underwriting the portfolio is more important than ever, which is why he says broker follow facilities and trackers are not of interest to the company. But I think what it does tell you is, if you’re going to write some of these trackers, probably the time to write the trackers is when the market is rock hard. Speaking during Lancashire Holdings’ analyst call today after the release of its third-quarter trading statement , Maloney said that selectivity is key in underwriting a portfolio in a softened insurance and reinsurance market, something he doesn’t believe is possible on a passive basis.

item.title: PIB Group names Aviva executive David Martin as incoming Group CEO
item.description: PIB Group, an international insurance intermediary specialising in insurance broking, managing general agents (MGAs) and other insurance services, has confirmed that David Martin will become its Group Chief Executive Officer in early 2027. Martin will move to the business from Aviva, where he currently holds the positions of Managing Director, UK Commercial and Chief Distribution Officer. He later joined Aviva in 2023, becoming a member of its UK General Insurance Executive Committee.

item.title: LMA CEO Sheila Cameron to step down in 2027 as search for successor gets under way
item.description: The Lloyd’s Market Association (LMA) has revealed that Sheila Cameron, who has led the organisation as Chief Executive Officer since 2019, will step down from the role, continuing in her position into early 2027 to ensure an orderly and seamless transition before taking on a new advisory role in the London market, while the process to appoint her successor is already underway. She went on, “I am incredibly proud of what we have achieved together, and of the role the Association continues to play in supporting a vibrant, innovative and successful Lloyd’s market.” “The LMA is in a strong position for the future with a talented leadership team, and I look forward to seeing the organisation continue to evolve and thrive under a new CEO.” Sean McGovern, Chair of the LMA, said, “Sheila has been an outstanding champion for the Association and the wider Lloyd’s market. Cameron said it has been an “enormous privilege” to serve as CEO of the LMA and to represent the interests of managing agents during a period of significant change for the market.

item.title: South Africa’s Kruger Park Faces Flood-Repair Funding Gap
item.description: South Africa’s iconic Kruger National Park faces a substantial funding shortfall to repair severe flood damage, restricting visitor numbers. Photograph: A flood-damaged road at Kruger National Park in February 2026; photo credit: Patrick van Katwijk/Getty Images The South African National Parks, the state entity that manages the reserve, has set aside 100 million rand and the national government 218 million rand, while there was a 150 million rand insurance settlement, but a gap of 481 million rand remains, he said in response to a parliamentary question.

item.title: European Supermarkets Rush to Patch Vulnerabilities After Region-Wide Fridge Hack
item.description: European supermarkets targeted in a second wave of cyberattacks that cranked up fridge and freezer temperatures were rushing on Tuesday to upgrade their systems and protect themselves against further hacking attempts. Stores in eight European countries were forced to throw away vast quantities of food after hackers tampered on Monday with their fridges, in an attack identical to one that swept dozens of supermarkets in France three weeks ago. Read more: Supermarkets Across Europe Report New Suspected Freezer Hack The seven stores hit by the attack are back up and running but their refrigeration systems have been disconnected from the internet, a spokesperson said.

item.title: 3M Commits $7.35 Billion to Settle PFAS-Related Claims
item.description: is committing $7.35 billion over nine years to settle litigation related to its use of chemicals known as PFAS. Last year, 3M reached an agreement to resolve PFAS-related claims in New Jersey. The company recorded a pre-tax charge of about $285 million and said it would make payments over 25 years related to PFAS-related claims in the state.

item.title: £4.9m seed round for i23, the AI-native insurance broker
item.description: Anand Sambasivan, Co-founder, i23, said: “We are building an AI-native insurance broker. According to Sky News, investors in the round are Outward VC, Seedcamp, Insiders VC and Four Cities Capital. Sambasivan’s LinkedIn post thanks the company’s investors but does not name them or give the size of the round.

item.title: Crestview Partners invests in Novel Financial Holdings
item.description: Novel Financial Holdings, a US underwriting and insurance services holding company, has secured an investment from private equity firm Crestview Partners. Crestview brings not only flexible capital but also meaningful sector expertise and relationships that will support our growth for years to come.” Dan Kilpatrick, Partner and Head of Financial Services at Crestview, said: “We are thrilled to be partnering with Rob and the terrific team at Novel. Rob Bredahl, Chief Executive Officer of Novel, said: “As we continue to scale and diversify Novel, we are excited to partner with Crestview, a firm that has been investing across insurance and reinsurance for two decades and has backed insurance businesses through full market cycles.

item.title: $43m funding for Lazarus AI with participation from QBE and State Farm Ventures
item.description: Investors participating include QBE, Mucker Capital, Motivate Ventures, State Farm Ventures, Wave Function Ventures, Indelible Solutions, Joyance Partners, AllegisNL Capital, One Way Ventures, AngelList, Techstars, Plug and Play, and others. Lazarus AI, the Boston-headquartered enterprise AI company, has announced $43m in funding, according to the release. Lazarus AI said it will use the funding to expand strategic partnerships, invest in research and development, and bring new products to market.

item.title: Gallagher Re selects Scrub AI
item.description: Gallagher Re has licensed Scrub AI to automate the cleaning and preparation of property binder bordereaux and exposure data for catastrophe modelling. Scrub AI will clean, validate and standardize incoming bordereaux and schedules of values into formats ready for catastrophe models. The platform will apply Gallagher Re’s data standards and modelling assumptions, while allowing its teams to control how data is mapped, coded and validated.

item.title: Windward acquires Azimut.ai
item.description: Maritime intelligence company Windward has acquired Azimut.ai , adding visual vessel identification technology to its platform. Azimut’s technology uses cameras at ports and maritime chokepoints to identify vessels in real time, including those that switch off their tracking signals to avoid detection. The acquisition marks Windward’s first move into ground- and ship-based sensors.

item.title: QBE and State Farm Ventures back Lazarus AI
item.description: QBE Ventures and State Farm Ventures participated in $43 million in funding announced by Lazarus AI . Other investors include Mucker Capital, Motivate Ventures, Wave Function Ventures, Indelible Solutions, Joyance Partners, AllegisNL Capital, One Way Ventures, AngelList, Techstars and Plug and Play. Lazarus partnered with Unqork to integrate AI-powered claims audits into insurance workflows, with the companies saying the system can review each claim in about two minutes and send exceptions to human reviewers.

item.title: APCIA Says Claims Data Standards in Works to Better Combat Criticism
item.description: Bell said APCIA is developing a standardized claims-closed data-call template. Two senators followed up the reports by sending letters to some of the largest insurers, asking for claims data. These days the insurance industry is “caught in the crosshairs,” and it may also be caught flatfooted – responding to recent scrutiny of a policy’s worth rather than working from in front with appropriate data.

item.title: Erasing Unmodeled Marine Risk: A Strategic Framework for CUOs
item.description: For decades, property/casualty carriers have relied on a singular technological foundation to price marine risk and establish geographic accumulation: the Automatic Identification System, or AIS. Originally designed as a localized collision avoidance tool for vessel masters, AIS was rapidly adopted by the commercial marine insurance sector as the de facto standard for global fleet tracking. Underwriters built their portfolios, modeled their catastrophe exposure, and deployed capacity based on where a vessel’s digital signal indicated it was operating.

item.title: Vantage Launches Facultative Reinsurance Business, Names Pickard as President
item.description: Vantage Group Holdings Ltd., the Bermuda-based re/insurer, announced the launch of its Facultative Reinsurance line of business, led by industry executive Lisa Pickard, who has joined Vantage as president of Facultative Reinsurance. She will build the team, define the underwriting approach, and develop broker and client relationships for the Facultative Reinsurance business. This expansion marks a key milestone in Vantage’s strategy to scale its specialty insurance and reinsurance lines following its June 2026 acquisition by Howard Hughes Holdings Inc.

item.title: Aon, Munich Re Launch Pandemic Reinsurance Solution in Asia
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) Aon (Dublin) and Munich Re (Munich) have launched a pandemic reinsurance solution designed to provide coverage for non-damage business interruption losses in Indonesia and the Philippines. Aon will access dedicated pandemic capacity for clients, while Munich Re will provide reinsurance capital, pricing and policy wordings. “The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the protection gap for this peril, particularly for non-damage business interruption losses,” comments Soeren Soltysiak, CEO of Asia, Reinsurance Solutions, Aon.
